title: phUSD-is-stake-AND-reward creates a structural conflict-of-interest: every claim mints fresh phUSD supply but increases the desired-APY denominator only if restaked, so accounting incentivises owner inflation
rootCause: phUSD is both the staking asset AND a freshly-minted reward stream. The phUSD-side reward rate is `phUSDPerSecond = totalStaked * desiredAPYBps / 10000 / SECONDS_PER_YEAR`, so the absolute mint rate scales linearly with `totalStaked`. When a staker claims, fresh phUSD is minted DIRECTLY TO the staker (not into the contract, so `totalStaked` doesn't increase). If the staker restakes the claimed phUSD, `totalStaked` increases, and so does the absolute mint rate -- a positive feedback loop bounded only by the staker's willingness to compound and the owner-controlled `desiredAPYBps`.
economicImpact: Two structural concerns: (a) the protocol's APY is denominated in the same token being minted, so the real APY (after dilution) is meaningfully lower than the stated APY -- e.g. 'we pay 100% APY in phUSD' is only true if phUSD's value remains constant, which it can't if 100% of TVL is being newly minted every year. The published `desiredAPYBps` overstates the real yield. (b) The compounding spiral means that a staker who never withdraws ends up holding a growing fraction of total phUSD supply -- 'rich get richer' in nominal phUSD terms. Combined with ECON-001 (uncapped APY), this means an owner who pre-stakes and compounds captures an exponentially-growing share of phUSD supply.
affectedParties: Non-staker phUSD holders (dilution); short-term stakers vs long-term compounders; the phUSD peg (if phUSD targets a stable value, the unconstrained mint pressure is a peg risk).
attackScenario: Owner sets desiredAPYBps to a 'normal' but generous value (e.g. 5_000 = 50% APY).
Owner stakes a large initial position from a wallet they control. Other stakers also enter.
Owner periodically calls `claim()` and `stake()` (or simply `stake(0)` would skip due to MINIMUM_STAKE; uses `stake(MINIMUM_STAKE)` plus claimed amount).
Over time, owner's share of `totalStaked` grows faster than other stakers' (because owner is the most diligent compounder, knowing the protocol best).
After many cycles, owner's share dominates `totalStaked`, so a disproportionate fraction of every future mint flows to them -- without any explicit 'attack'.

Variant: if the published APY attracts more honest stakers, the absolute phUSD mint rate per unit time grows linearly with TVL, accelerating phUSD supply expansion. This is unsustainable in the long run -- phUSD value must drop (if it floats) or the mint must be subsidised by an external source (if pegged).
profitability: For the compounding staker: profit = (apy_nominal - apy_real) * stake_size * time, where the gap is the dilution rate. For the owner with pre-staked dominance: profit ~= TVL_growth * owner_share - owner_initial_stake.
preconditions: phUSD has no external supply ceiling that would cap mints (or has a ceiling but it's high relative to TVL).
The phUSD value-anchor (peg or backing) is sensitive to supply expansion.
Owner / sophisticated stakers can compound; passive stakers do not.

intentMismatchEvidence.documentation: Profile §8.5: 'Token-asset overlap (phUSD as both stake and reward) ... No invariant violation; flag for econ-scanner.' The submodule CLAUDE.md positions this as a 'staking yield farm' but doesn't address the dilution problem or specify whether phUSD has a supply cap or a peg.
intentMismatchEvidence.implementation: `_claimRewards` mints phUSD without any reference to total supply or value-anchor; `_updatePhUSDEmissionRate` scales the mint rate linearly with `totalStaked` (the feedback is mathematical, not capped).
intentMismatchEvidence.discrepancy: A 'yield farm' for a stablecoin (phUSD) where the yield itself is newly-minted stablecoin is fundamentally a self-referential incentive. Without an exogenous source of phUSD value (collateral, fees, etc.), the published APY is nominal-only; the protocol implements a money-printer disguised as a yield product.

mitigations: Cap phUSD mint per unit time at the IFlax / governance layer (not in this contract, but document the dependency).
Source the phUSD-side rewards from an external sink (e.g. fees collected elsewhere) instead of fresh mints; or have the stable-yield-accumulator fund both legs.
Publish a 'real APY net of dilution' metric in docs alongside the nominal APY.
Add a per-block global mint cap on this contract (e.g. require `totalMintedToday < cap`) so compounding spirals are bounded even if the owner mis-sets APY.
crossReferences: ECON-001 (uncapped APY) - amplifier: the compounding spiral is bounded by APY; with uncapped APY, the spiral is unbounded.
